---
title: "Ensure data integrity with constraints"
description: "Prevent invalid data by applying rules to your table columns using PostgreSQL constraints"
products: [cloud, self_hosted]
---

import * as C from "@constants";
import { Callout } from "@stainless-api/docs/components";
import TestPlan from "@components/TestPlan.astro";

Constraints reject invalid rows at insert or update time. On {C.HYPERTABLE}s, {C.TIMESCALE_DB} mirrors those rules to underlying {C.CHUNK}s and keeps related indexes consistent when you add, change, or drop a constraint.

{C.HYPERTABLE}s support all standard {C.PG} constraint types. For foreign keys in particular, the following is supported:

- Foreign key constraints from a {C.HYPERTABLE} referencing a regular table
- Foreign key constraints from a regular table referencing a {C.HYPERTABLE}

Foreign keys from a {C.HYPERTABLE} referencing another {C.HYPERTABLE} **are not supported**.

For example, you can create a table that only allows positive device IDs, and
non-null temperature readings. You can also check that time values for all
devices are unique. To create this table, with the constraints, use this
command:

```sql
CREATE TABLE conditions (
    time       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    temp       FLOAT NOT NULL,
    device_id  INTEGER CHECK (device_id > 0),
    location   INTEGER REFERENCES locations (id),
    PRIMARY KEY(time, device_id)
) WITH (
    tsdb.hypertable
);
```

This example also references values in another `locations` table using a foreign
key constraint.

<Callout variant="note">

Time columns used for partitioning must not allow `NULL` values. A
`NOT NULL` constraint is added by default to these columns if it doesn't already exist.

</Callout>

For more information on how to manage constraints, see the [{C.PG} docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html).

<TestPlan>
target: cloud, self-hosted

1. fork the service
2. [cloud] select the service
3. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;`
4. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE locations (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, city TEXT);`
5. run SQL: `INSERT INTO locations VALUES (1, 'Oslo');`
6. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE conditions (time TIMESTAMPTZ, temp FLOAT NOT NULL, device_id INTEGER CHECK (device_id > 0), location INTEGER REFERENCES locations (id), PRIMARY KEY(time, device_id)) WITH (tsdb.hypertable);`
7. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM timescaledb_information.hypertables WHERE hypertable_name = 'conditions'`
8. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid = 'conditions'::regclass AND contype IN ('c', 'f', 'p') HAVING count(*) = 3`
9. run SQL: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES ('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00', 20.5, 1, 1);`
10. expect error containing `conditions_device_id_check`: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES ('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00', 20.5, 0, 1)`
11. expect error containing `not-null constraint`: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES ('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00', NULL, 2, 1)`
12. expect error containing `conditions_pkey`: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES ('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00', 21.0, 1, 1)`
13. expect error containing `conditions_location_fkey`: `INSERT INTO conditions VALUES ('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00', 20.5, 3, 99)`
14. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE condition_notes (time TIMESTAMPTZ, device_id INTEGER, note TEXT, FOREIGN KEY (time, device_id) REFERENCES conditions (time, device_id));`
15. run SQL: `INSERT INTO condition_notes VALUES ('2026-01-01 00:00:00+00', 1, 'calibrated');`
16. expect error containing `condition_notes_time_device_id_fkey`: `INSERT INTO condition_notes VALUES ('2026-01-02 00:00:00+00', 5, 'orphan')`
17. expect error containing `foreign key references of hypertables`: `CREATE TABLE condition_events (time TIMESTAMPTZ, device_id INTEGER, event TEXT, FOREIGN KEY (time, device_id) REFERENCES conditions (time, device_id)) WITH (tsdb.hypertable)`
18. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE readings (time TIMESTAMPTZ, reading INTEGER) WITH (tsdb.hypertable);`
19. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'readings' AND column_name = 'time' AND is_nullable = 'NO'`
</TestPlan>
